metadata.description: Hatsu — the local plane of the Akatsuki system, and the way of working itself. Kurapika (/kurapika) leads in six declared Nen-type work-modes, named per reply; Gon, Hisoka, Phinks and Uvogin stand beside him as ratified independents. Twenty-seven skills at v0.4.0: seventeen drive backlogs, PRs, releases and QA on deterministic Nen verbs, and ten are the local loop itself — breath, rasengan, kokusen, amaterasu, tsukuyomi, rikugan, jutaisho, ao, aka and ren. Two config files hold every parameter, two harness hooks ring the bell and refuse a commit on the trunk, and five phases stay yours to call. Runs on your own credentials — no App, no bot identity. Hard dependency on the Nen CLI, checked at warm-up and failing closed with auto-install.

plugins.description: Hatsu — the local plane of the Akatsuki system, and the way of working itself. Kurapika (/kurapika) leads in six declared Nen-type work-modes, named per reply — Enhancer (product code), Conjurer (canon & governance), Transmuter (machinery), Manipulator (GitHub-side ops), Emitter (release & fan-out), Specialist (product intake). Gon is the mission-scoped delegate who crosses no gate until his delegation grammar is ratified; Hisoka reviews UI/UX and measures quality before a PR posts; Phinks runs adversarial pre-release QA on proven findings; Uvogin measures the fixed seven performance metrics with method blocks and baselines. Feitan and Chrollo were activated from the bench on 2026-09-09, definitions due at v0.5.0; Killua and the other five bench profiles are recorded OPEN. Twenty-seven skills ship aboard. Seventeen answer a request — backlog-state, backlog-board, backlog-loop, backlog-synthesis, bankai-handbooks, bankai-quality, build, drive, file, futon, getsuga, izanagi, izanami, jujisho, pr-state, senkei, tensho. Ten are the loop: breath (warm-up and the branch), rasengan (build before every commit), kokusen (commit, with an ask on every flagged file), amaterasu (launch from your own working directory), tsukuyomi (tests), rikugan (the rich HTML report), jutaisho (the bell), ao (pull from the base), aka (push — yours to call) and ren (the per-request loop, which never pushes). Every deterministic step is a Nen verb, with per-skill evidence in docs/ab/. Policy lives in nen/workflow.json and execution in nen/contract.json's project block (docs/WORKFLOW.md explains both); hooks/hooks.json rings the stop bell and refuses a commit or a push on the base branch. No AI attribution trailer is ever recorded — Akatsuki-Agent is the single admitted one. Runs on your own credentials — no App, no bot identity. Hard dependency on the Nen CLI, checked at warm-up against nen/contract.json, failing closed with auto-install.
